transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, thank you for fitting me in. I suppose what brings me in is that my sleep has just become completely unmoored. It’s entirely off the tracks. 

At first, I was waking up after only two or three hours, but I felt fantastic—completely ready to go. I was up drafting all these elaborate plans. I actually started redesigning the entire layout of my library. I have thousands of books from my university days, you know, mostly historical sociology and a few rare editions, and I realized standard cataloging is completely inadequate. So I was up at 2 AM with a ruler and graph paper, drafting a new system based on thematic resonance... My wife thought I was being ridiculous, but she doesn't understand the importance of spatial memory when dealing with complex texts. 

But, ah, what was I saying? Right, the sleeping. Well, now it's shifted. Now, I just lie awake for hours before dawn. My stomach gets so tight, just tied in knots, and I get absolutely no sense of rest at all. It actually reminds me of how my stomach felt right before I defended my dissertation back in Chicago. Have you ever been to Chicago in February? The wind coming off the lake just cuts right through your coat, it doesn't matter what you're wearing, you just freeze to the bone... anyway, yes, I just can't seem to get any real rest now.
Right now, during this period of poor sleep, would you say your overall mood has been low or sad, or do you still feel elevated, irritable, or full of energy at times?

Low. Very, very low. The energy is completely gone now. When I'm lying there awake in the dark, I just... I keep replaying this investment decision I made recently. It just loops in my head, and I keep telling myself I have completely ruined my wife’s financial security. I feel like such an absolute fool, especially after a lifetime of being the responsible one. 

Being the responsible one was always my defining trait, you know? My grandfather actually instilled that in me—he worked at a bank in Philadelphia for forty years. He used to wear these incredible three-piece suits every single day, even in the dead of summer. You just don't see tailoring like that anymore. The wool they used back then had a completely different weight to it, it draped so much better than the synthetic blends people buy off the rack today. And the buttons were real horn, not plastic. I actually have one of his old pocket watches, a beautiful Waltham piece, though the mainspring needs replacing... 

But... anyway, yes. I just lie there feeling like a complete failure. A lifetime of being careful, and I've just thrown her security away.

When you think about this investment decision and feeling like you've ruined your wife's financial security, do you believe that with complete certainty—even if she or others reassure you otherwise—or do you recognize that you might be overestimating how bad things really are?

Oh, I know it with absolute certainty. She tries to reassure me, she really does, but... I just keep replaying the investment decision over and over in my head. I keep telling myself I have completely ruined my wife’s security. And I've made an absolute fool of a lifetime of being the responsible one. It's just devastating. 

We had these municipal bonds, you see... and municipal bonds used to be the absolute bedrock of a proper portfolio. I actually remember reading a fascinating sociological paper on the history of municipal debt in the 19th century—how cities funded the first major sewer systems. Public health was completely transformed because of those bonds. Take London's cholera outbreak in 1854, for instance. John Snow mapping the Broad Street pump... brilliant work, really, just mapping out the water supply and proving the disease wasn't caused by miasma in the air. Water infrastructure is entirely underappreciated today, people just turn on the tap and expect... 

Wait. I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Ah, the reassurance. Yes. No, I don't think I'm overestimating how bad it is. I really have ruined it all.
